To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a small number of users in an online social network are highly influential, (ii) the influence of a user on the adoption behavior of other users in the network decays as the social distance between the two users increases, and (iii) the influence of users is not uniform and is dependent on the type of the user’s influence.

(1) the influence of a given user on a target user is positively correlated with the similarity of their tastes; (2) the influence of the user on the target user increases as the target user’s exposure to the user increases; (3) the influence of users who are similar to the target user is greater than the influence of those who are less similar; and (4) users with higher levels of taste similarity tend to be more influential.
